prompt: Det ___ regna imorgon.
hint: It’s going to rain tomorrow. (a prediction)
explain: Nobody decides the weather, so use kommer att for a prediction.

prompt: Jag ___ att Anna har en ny pojkvän.
hint: I think Anna has a new boyfriend. (a guess, I’m not sure)
explain: When you believe something but aren’t sure, use tror.

prompt: Du ___ älska Lappland!
hint: You’re going to love Lapland! (my prediction)
explain: You can’t plan to love a place, so a prediction about feelings takes kommer att.

prompt: Hon ___ bli trött efter den långa resan.
hint: She’ll be tired after the long trip. (a prediction)
explain: Nobody decides to get tired, so use kommer att for a prediction.

prompt: Det ___ bli dyrt att renovera köket.
hint: It’s going to be expensive to renovate the kitchen. (a prediction)
explain: A guess about how things will turn out takes kommer att.

prompt: Om du tränar varje dag, kommer du ___ bli starkare.
hint: If you train every day, you will get stronger.
explain: The prediction form is always kommer att + infinitive.

prompt: Jag ___ laga pasta ikväll. Vill du komma?
hint: I’m going to cook pasta tonight. (my plan) Do you want to come?
explain: Use ska for plans. Ska is a help verb, so the infinitive follows directly, with no att.

prompt: Vi ___ äta middag hos Lena på lördag.
hint: We’re having dinner at Lena’s on Saturday. (it’s planned)
explain: A plan takes ska + infinitive, with no att.

prompt: ___ vi gå på bio ikväll?
hint: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?
explain: Ska vi …? is how you suggest a plan: shall we …?

prompt: Jag ___ till tandläkaren klockan tre.
hint: I’m going to the dentist at three. (I have an appointment)
explain: Ska can stand alone with a direction (ska till …); kommer att always needs a verb after it.

prompt: Jag ___ till Helsingfors imorgon.
hint: I’m going to Helsinki tomorrow.
explain: Present tense + a time word like imorgon talks about the future.

prompt: Kursen ___ på måndag.
hint: The course starts next Monday.
explain: Present tense + a time word like på måndag talks about the future.

prompt: Jag ___ sluta röka efter nyår.
hint: I intend to quit smoking after New Year.
explain: Tänker + infinitive shows an intention: I intend to.

prompt: Vad tänker du ___ i sommar?
hint: What are you planning to do this summer?
explain: Tänker meaning intend is followed by the infinitive without att.

prompt: Jag har sett filmen. Jag ___ att den är bra.
hint: I’ve seen the film. In my opinion it’s good.
explain: An opinion about something you have seen or tried takes tycker.

prompt: Jag ___ att bussen går klockan åtta, men jag är inte säker.
hint: I think the bus leaves at eight, but I’m not sure.
explain: When you aren’t sure if something is true, use tror.

prompt: Jag ___ på dig.
hint: I’m thinking of you.
explain: Thinking about someone is tänka på.

prompt: Jag ___ inte om fisk.
hint: I don’t like fish.
explain: Like is tycka om: Jag tycker om …, Jag tycker inte om …

prompt: ___ du att det blir sol i helgen?
hint: Do you think it will be sunny this weekend? (a guess)
explain: Nobody can know the weather yet, so a guess about it takes tror.

prompt: Jag ___ att svenska är ett vackert språk.
hint: In my opinion, Swedish is a beautiful language.
explain: A personal opinion or taste takes tycker.

sentence: Jag ska börja en kurs i januari.
accept: I januari ska jag börja en kurs.
en: I’m going to start a course in January.
explain: Ska is the verb in second place; the infinitive börja comes after the subject.
Kommer is the verb in second place, and att + infinitive follows.

prompt: Det ___ bli varmt i helgen. (is going to – a prediction)
hint: It’s going to be warm this weekend.
explain: A prediction about the weather takes kommer att.

prompt: Vi ___ till Åland på fredag. (are going – a plan)
hint: We’re going to Åland on Friday.
explain: A plan with a direction can be just ska + till …: Vi ska till Åland.

prompt: Jag ___ att det blir en bra fest. (think – a guess)
hint: I think it will be a good party.
explain: A guess about the future takes tror.

prompt: Jag ___ att kaffet är för starkt. (think – my opinion)
hint: I think the coffee is too strong.
explain: An opinion about something you have tasted takes tycker.

prompt: Vad tänker du ___ ikväll? (do)
hint: What are you planning to do tonight?
explain: Tänker is followed by the infinitive without att: tänker göra.

prompt: Jag ___ ofta på min familj. (think about)
hint: I often think about my family.
explain: Thinking about someone is tänka på.

prompt: När jag var liten ___ jag att tomten fanns på riktigt.
hint: When I was little, I believed that Santa Claus was real.
explain: A belief, in the past: tro → trodde.

prompt: Jag såg filmen igår. Jag ___ att den var rolig.
hint: I saw the film yesterday. In my opinion it was funny.
explain: An opinion from experience, in the past: tycka → tyckte.
